A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 14 pages of v3 and 16 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original recursive-training experiments with GPT-2 and SmolLM2, detector evaluations on MAGE, and collapse-mitigation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains original training and detection results and adds experiments with additional SmolLM2 sizes and supplementary detector and distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The reported parameter-selection procedure changes: v3 derives the sampling exponent b from the detector threshold and fixes the duplication cap at 10; v5 selects both parameters using validation performance and makes the cap model-specific. The detector architecture, normalized weighting formula and 1.5-fold resampling remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 trains detectors on MAGE alone. v5 Appendix B.3 adds a RAID subset to detector training for SmolLM2, incorporating multiple decoding strategies and adversarially modified texts. This substantially expands detector-training conditions; the WikiText-2 generation task and existing MAGE evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding mitigation experiments retain the all-data baseline and human-only Oracle. Table 2 evaluates the same RoBERTa, DeBERTav3 and ModernBERT detectors. The added model-size experiments reuse the existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: v5 adds SmolLM2 135M and 1.7B configurations and reports balanced, source-separated RAID splits. Detector checkpoint selection changes from v3's macro-F1 criterion with early stopping to highest validation AUC over five epochs. Resampling parameters are now selected on WikiText-2 validation data after one generation. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds detector-score distributions before and after resampling (Figure S2), SmolLM2 perplexity-distribution analysis (Figure S3), and model-size sensitivity experiments (Figure S5). These extend v3's decoding, mixing and GPT-2 distribution analyses with substantive evidence about resampling behavior and scale dependence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify detector seed 42. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added histograms describe sample distributions rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: SmolLM2 results are extensively revised in Tables 1, 3 and the detailed appendix table; for example, greedy generation-9 perplexity changes from 90.24 to 85.69. v5 adds 135M/1.7B results and diagnostic findings. GPT-2 and Table 2 scores remain unchanged. Revised mitigation results involve changed settings, while Figure 1 inconsistently retains v3's curves.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix C.1 defines b = 1 + threshold/(1 - threshold) and provides an odds-ratio justification. v5 removes this mathematical rule and reasoning in favor of validation-based selection. Equations 1–4 remain unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion extend the validation claim to model sizes spanning 124M–1.7B. The central claims about decoding-dependent collapse, detector-guided prevention and possible improvements over human-only training remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds an explicit limitation linking resampling quality and generalizability to detector errors, biases, domains, architectures and decoding strategies. It removes v3's small-model limitation and speculation about greater benefits for larger models, and introduces an SIR interpretation. The fine-tuning and task-generalization caveats remain.

D1.justification: v5 adds source-code and detector-checkpoint links, temperature-calibration details using L-BFGS for 50 iterations at learning rate 0.01, RAID construction instructions, and a model-specific resampling table. However, v3's explicit evaluation batch size, no-warm-up statement and classification-threshold selection instructions are omitted.

R1.justification: v5 adds Wang et al. and Hsieh et al. to distinguish curated synthetic training from uncontrolled recursion, Dugan et al. for RAID, and Rubin for SIR. It removes the Strong Model Collapse citation. The central positioning around unknown data origins remains; bibliographic renaming and CCNet deduplication are not new research relationships.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work, resampling and results passages undergo substantial rewriting. Decoding background becomes a separate section, and the appendices are reorganized to place recursive training before detection and rearrange detector documentation. These changes extend beyond renumbering or the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: v5 adds diagnostic and scale-comparison figures plus a hyperparameter table, expands the result tables, and redesigns Figure S1 from GPT-2 pure-sampling plots to paired top-k plots for both models. Existing appendix mitigation figures become S4/S6 with revised SmolLM2 panels, substantially reorganizing the appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The added scale tests and detector diagnostics strengthen empirical support, while explicit detector limitations, calibration details and code/checkpoint links improve transparency and reproducibility. These constitute a limited net gain. Quantitative consistency worsens because v5 revises SmolLM2 values in Table 1 while retaining v3's Figure 1 curves, although the principal qualitative findings remain stable.
